props.title: One musician, the piano, and a voice when you want one.

rows.text: When the venue has a piano, the pianist plays it, and a hotel lobby or a club dining space usually has one. When it doesn’t, a stage piano comes with the booking, and from the tables it sounds like a piano in the corner.

On its own the piano is instrumental, which is the version most client dinners and galas book. When the evening wants singing, a voice joins for a set or for the night, on the same line of the contract.

props.html: For a bigger crowd, a jazz duo plays the same hours. When the night wants a dance floor after dinner, a band or the DJ takes over through the same sound system on the same contract. The rest of the covers list is on the repertoire page.

rows.text: Twenty at one table or eighty at ten, in a private dining space or a club, where the conversation is the event.
The doors and the dinner, before the program. Gala entertainment ideas has the smaller gala where the piano is the whole evening.
A holiday party that’s a dinner rather than a dance floor, or the January office party after the December rush.
A jazz brunch at a club, a hotel or a restaurant, with standards under the whole service.
The prelude as people arrive, and the songs the family chooses, when the chapel or the reception has a piano.
A standing afternoon at a community, with the residents’ own songs from the Great American Songbook.
A house with a piano in it, and a table of twelve.

props.html: Stage sizes and power are on the technical page, and the questions every booking shares, from substitutions to volume limits, are on the full question list.

items.a: Standards and covers, from the Great American Songbook to Elton John and Billy Joel, played through arrival, cocktails and dinner. The set can lean jazz, lean pop or move between the two as the evening goes on. It's booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

items.q: Does the venue need a piano?
items.a: No. When the venue has one, the pianist plays it, and it only needs the tuning the venue already keeps up. When it doesn't, a stage piano and a small sound system come with the booking, set up in a corner of about 6 by 4 feet with one dedicated 20-amp circuit and 45 minutes to set up.

About as loud as the conversation at the table, so two people across from each other hear each other and the piano both. A pianist sets the level to the space: in a small dining space the stage piano plays barely amplified, and in a ballroom the sound support carries it to the back tables without getting loud at the front ones.

items.q: Can we ask for a song, or add time?
items.a: Yes. If you want a song that isn't on the list, let us know when you book and we can usually learn it, and if you think the dinner might run long, let us know that too. An announcement microphone is ready for the toast or the remarks.
